title: Processes vs threads
hook: Processes are isolated programs. Threads are workers that share one process’s memory.

steps.caption: Process A and Process B don’t share memory — a bad pointer in A shouldn’t trash B.

nodeCaptions.p2: Talking across processes needs explicit IPC — pipes, sockets, etc.

steps.caption: Inside Process A, two threads share the same heap. They can both touch the same data.

nodeCaptions.t1: Lightweight: same process, separate call stack.
nodeCaptions.t2: Sharing is power and danger — races live here.

takeaways: Processes isolate; threads share an address space.
Threads are cheaper to create/switch, but need synchronization.
Pick process boundaries for safety, threads for shared-memory parallelism.

quiz.question: Why can two threads corrupt the same variable more easily than two processes?
choices: Threads share memory by default; processes don’t
Processes can’t run at the same time
quiz.explanation: Shared heap = concurrent access unless you coordinate.
